messages:

Cc: procurements@tilewave.com
Date: 2027-11-07 15:12 PST
Subject: Re: Order form details - invoicing cadence and tax allocation

Hi Karthik / Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week — TileWave is excited to move forward. Before we circulate a PO, finance has two sticking points on the order form we need to resolve:

1) Invoicing cadence / entity split: our treasury requires invoices split between TileWave, Inc. (US) for hosted usage and TileWave EMEA Ltd for EU-based seats. Can we get line-item invoicing by legal entity?

2) Net terms / proration: we generally run Net45 across vendor contracts. Would Redwood accept Net45 for the initial 12-month term? Also we may seasonally ramp usage; would Redwood support proration for mid-quarter add-ons?

Finally, our tax team flagged VAT handling for EU entities — they expect Redwood to provide VAT invoices where applicable but may need evidence of tax registration. Can you share what evidence you can provide?

If you can send an updated order form and MSA redlines, procurement will review and aim to return a PO within 3 business days.

Thanks,
Maria Lopez
Head of Procurement
TileWave

Attachment: none (see requested docs)
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-11-08 09:18 PST
Subject: Re: Order form details - invoicing cadence and tax allocation

Hi Maria — appreciate the clarity. Quick responses inline and a proposal attached.

1) Entity split: we can generate separate invoices per legal entity. Practically we will need PO numbers and billing addresses for each entity to populate the invoice header. I've attached TileWave_OrderForm_Draft_v2.xlsx with separate line items mapped to each legal entity (US vs EMEA).

2) Net terms: Standard Redwood hosted customers are on Net30. For strategic accounts we can accept Net45 for the first 12-month commitment if the deal signs an approved payment schedule. I'd like to propose a phased-commit approach to reduce administrative churn:
   - Month 1-3: 50% of initial commit invoiced upfront (prepaid) to cover capacity reservation.
   - Month 4-12: remaining committed amount invoiced monthly/quarterly on Net45.
This gives TileWave initial runway while aligning Redwood on capacity planning. See the attached OrderForm_payflow_proposal_20271108.docx for the example schedule.

3) VAT and tax evidence: Redwood can provide VAT invoices for EU-registered entities and a VAT registration certificate for our EU billing entity. If TileWave needs additional tax residency letters or W-8/W-9 equivalents for the US entity, we can supply them — I'll loop in Legal to confirm exact docs.

Kimberly — can you review the attached MSA redline scope? Key asks from TileWave: Net45 acceptance, separate-entity invoicing, and proration language for add-ons. I flagged the payment schedule as a commercial concession.

Maria — if the proposed phasing looks acceptable, I can send the MSA redline PDF and an updated order form for signature (DocuSign).

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0198

Date: 2027-11-08 14:06 PST
Subject: Re: Order form details - invoicing cadence and tax allocation

Karthik / Laura — reviewed Maria's asks and Karthik's proposal. High-level legal notes:

- Net terms: Legal will sign off on Net45 for the initial 12-month term provided: (a) a payment schedule (already proposed) is attached to the Order Form as a schedule; and (b) Redwood retains a shortfall remedy (credit/true-up or invoice acceleration) if TileWave falls behind more than 60 days on cumulative committed payments.

- Entity invoicing: We can support per-entity invoicing but need a contractual mapping table in the Order Form that lists (1) legal entity name; (2) billing address; (3) tax ID/VAT number; (4) PO number. We'll add a Billing Appendix to the Order Form.

- Proration: We accept proration for mid-term add-ons; will define "proration" as credit/charge applied to the next invoice and preserve minimum commit accounting (i.e., adds increase committed usage prospectively).

- VAT evidence: Finance will provide a VAT registration certificate for Redwood's EU entity. We can't warrant customer-specific VAT classification — customer must provide its VAT ID for validation.

I've prepared a short redline (MSA_redline_kp_20271108.pdf) that: (i) adds a Billing Appendix reference; (ii) inserts the payment schedule; and (iii) clarifies remedies for non-payment. Please review and confirm if the acceleration clause language is acceptable commercially.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai

- Proration language added for mid-term add-ons; committed floor maintained for minimums.
- Non-payment remedy: acceleration if cumulative outstanding exceeds 60 days.

Next steps: if procurement confirms the PO numbers and entity billing addresses, we will: (1) populate the Billing Appendix; (2) generate separate invoices during execution; (3) send DocuSign envelope for MSA + Order Form. I've included a draft DocuSign envelope link in related links.
